USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Falling sodium

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 72-year-old woman starts carbamazepine and develops confusion and unsteadiness. Sodium is 122 mmol/L, plasma osmolality is low, and urine remains inappropriately concentrated. She appears euvolemic. Which medication effect best explains these findings?

  1. Osmotic diuresis from hyperglycemia
  2. Acute calcium-channel blockade in the heart
  3. SIADH-associated hyponatremia
  4. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
  5. Mineralocorticoid excess
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

SIADH-associated hyponatremia

Carbamazepine can cause inappropriate antidiuresis and hyponatremia, especially in susceptible older patients.

Understanding the options

SIADH-associated hyponatremia
Carbamazepine can cause inappropriate antidiuresis and hyponatremia, especially in susceptible older patients.
Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
This produces dilute urine and often hypernatremia.
Mineralocorticoid excess
This does not explain euvolemic hypotonic hyponatremia with concentrated urine.
Osmotic diuresis from hyperglycemia
The described pattern is inappropriate water retention rather than glucose-driven diuresis.
Acute calcium-channel blockade in the heart
This does not explain the biochemical pattern.
